idiom_name: use { } on Closeable (kotlin.io.use) with an owner-side release
implementation_notes: kotlin.io's use extension is the stdlib scope function that guarantees the release: pool.acquire().use { r -> ... } closes r on every exit path. The hand-back semantics still belong to the owner - the object's close returns it to the pool - so a lending API should return an AutoCloseable whose close hands back, or better, expose a lambda-taking helper (pool.withConnection { c -> ... }) so the borrower never sees a release method at all. The classic C++ wrapper structure is needed only when the resource must travel beyond the lexical block, which is exactly what use cannot express.
pitfalls: use calls close() and appends its failure as a suppressed exception to the body's, so a throwing hand-back turns a completed operation into a failure; keep release-side close non-throwing.
use is inline and non-suspending: an asynchronous hand-back needs try/finally around the suspend body (or a suspend-aware helper), because there is no await use equivalent.
Nullable receivers and explicit close() calls bypass use entirely; acquiring into a nullable and closing later risks a silent no-op and a leaked pool slot.
